title: To prevent potential shortage: Govt must prepare alternative fuel plans – Attanayake
summary: By Naalir Jamaldeen Tissa Attanayake, National Organiser of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), yesterday (3), urged the Government to prepare alternative plans to meet the country’s fuel demand once the current one-month stock runs out. Addressing the media in Colombo, Attanayake said that while the Government has assured the public of sufficient fuel stocks for a month, it must also be ready to prevent a potential shortage once those reserves are depleted. He noted that if adequate fuel stocks are available, the public need not panic. However, he cautioned that relying on imports from countries such as India and Singapore may not be a secure long-term solution, particularly if the ongoing conflict in the Middle East escalates and disrupts global fuel supplies. Attanayake stated that the SJB views the war in the Middle East with concern and hopes for its swift conclusion. He stressed that the Government must prioritise the safety and well-being of Sri Lankans employed in Middle Eastern countries. He highlighted several urgent matters requiring immediate attention, including protecting the lives and employment of Sri Lankan migrant workers in the Middle East, safeguarding foreign remittances sent by these workers, and ensuring the stability of tea exports, noting that nearly 25% of Sri Lanka’s tea exports are destined for Middle Eastern markets. Attanayake emphasised that it is the duty of the Opposition to advise the Government on properly managing national challenges. He rejected suggestions that such criticism amounts to political destabilisation. “As an Opposition party, we are obliged to point out mistakes with the aim of correcting them,” he said. He further clarified that the SJB does not encourage public unrest or fuel queues, instead urging citizens to avoid panic and conserve fuel where possible. title: Citing ‘serious safety risks’: U.S. citizens told to leave 14 Middle Eastern countries
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan The United States’ Department of State has urged Americans to immediately depart several countries in the Middle East using available commercial transportation, citing “serious safety risks” amid escalating tensions in the region. In a security update issued on 2 March, the department called on US citizens in affected areas to leave without delay and to make use of commercial travel options while they remain available. The advisory applies to Americans in Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, including the West Bank and Gaza, as well as Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. “Depart now via commercial means due to serious safety risks,” the notice stated. Americans requiring assistance in arranging their departure have been advised to contact the State Department’s 24-hour helplines (from the United States and Canada). The US citizens were also encouraged to enrol in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Programme (STEP) to receive the latest security updates from the nearest US embassy or consulate.

title: Chamari, Vishmi Power Sri Lanka to Comfortable Win over Pakistan
summary: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu fell just short of what could have been a magnificent century, but her blistering 94 ensured Sri Lanka cruised to a comfortable victory over Pakistan in their ICC Women’s T20 World Cup warm-up match at Derby today. Pakistan, batting first, posted 168 for 8, with Chethana Vimukthi starring for Sri Lanka’s bowling attack by claiming 4 for 31. In reply, Athapaththu and 20 year old Vishmi Gunarathne forged a commanding 159-run opening stand that all but sealed the game. Athapaththu, attempting to reach her century with a six, was dismissed for 94 off 58 balls  an innings decorated with nine fours and five sixes. Gunarathne, who showed intent early in the powerplay with a flurry of boundaries, remained unbeaten on 63 from 50 deliveries, striking four fours and three sixes. Her composed knock perfectly complemented Athapaththu’s fireworks, guiding Sri Lanka to a dominant finish.
